title: Neptune: The Long Orbit to Benchmarking Long Video Understanding

paper.authors: Nagrani, Menon, Iscen, Buch, Mehran, Jha, Hauth, Zhu, Smaira, Schmid, Sun, Angelova, Dave et al. (Google DeepMind / Google Research)
paper.venue: arXiv 2412.09582 (Dec 2024); dataset page now part of the MINERVA collection
paper.repo_license: Apache-2.0 for software, CC BY 4.0 for all other materials (README 'License and disclaimer')
paper.other_artifacts: The repository is data-only: README, six PNG figures and one JSON (minerva-ego_20260205.json). No evaluation code, no frame-extraction or ASR code, no model outputs. Annotations live in Google Cloud Storage. NEW (verified by this card): the README's storage.mtls.cloud.google.com links 302 to a Google sign-in, but the plain bucket URLs https://storage.googleapis.com/neptunedata/neptune_full.json (4,599,593 bytes) and .../neptune_mmh.json (1,665,552 bytes) return HTTP 200 without credentials.

dependence.note: GPT-4o is one of the benchmarked systems: the Table 4 row is a direct measurement of model outputs, with no human or LLM judge in the multiple-choice metric (the GEM column does use a Gemma-based open-ended metric, but the accuracy column does not). Gemini-1.5-pro was additionally used inside the semi-automatic dataset-creation pipeline, so the items themselves are partly model-generated, but they are frozen and released - only the evaluation arm would need re-running.

claim.statement: With 8 RGB frames plus the ASR transcript, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 answers NEPTUNE-FULL's 3,268 five-way MCQs at 80.23% accuracy and the harder vision-required subset NEPTUNE-MMH (1,171 MCQs) at 72.86%, on a par with Gemini-1.5-pro-002 at all frames + ASR (80.98 / 75.42) and far above the best open-source long-context MLLM (LLaVA-OneVision, 66.22 / 62.82) and the 20.00 random baseline (Table 4).
claim.metric: Multiple-choice accuracy: the model is asked to emit '[CHOICE]: [REASON]' and the chosen option is compared with answer_id over five options (answer plus four decoys). GEM (the second column) is a separate Gemma-based open-ended equivalence metric and is not needed for the accuracy claim.

original_values.caveat: The GEM value 49.01 is flagged in the Table 4 caption as '*Computed on 10% of the results'.

claim.original_source: Paper Table 4 (row 'GPT-4o4 RGB (8 frames) + ASR'), footnote 4 ('Version gpt-4o-2024-05-13'), Section 5.2 ('For GPT-4o we use the public API'), Section 3 dataset statistics. Release counts measured by the card author from the two bucket JSONs on 2026-09-19.

protocol.model_usage_verified: yes - footnote 4 pins the snapshot explicitly; no alias inference needed
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with multimodal content parts (8 image_url parts plus text)
protocol.prompt_source: Appendix C.5.6 'GPT-4o prompts', block 'Multiple-choice evaluation with transcript' (printed verbatim, including the duplicated 'and and')

params.frame_sampling: not reported for GPT-4o; the paper's other 8-frame baselines use uniform sampling, so uniform is the natural assumption
params.asr_engine: not reported; transcripts are not in the release

protocol.evaluation: Parse the text before the first ':' as the chosen option, match it against the five answer_choice_i strings (or their index/letter), compare with answer_id, and report accuracy. No judge, no logprobs. Choice presentation (letters vs raw answer text vs numbering) is not printed in the paper.
protocol.environment: Would require: YouTube video download for 2,189 video ids, decoding and uniform 8-frame extraction, an ASR pass, and a multimodal request builder. None of this exists in the repository.

artifacts.prompts_path: paper Appendix C.5.6 only - not in the repository
artifacts.data_path: https://storage.googleapis.com/neptunedata/neptune_full.json (2,974 rows) and neptune_mmh.json (1,074 rows); fields key / video_id / question / answer_choice_0..4 / answer_id / answer / question_type. Videos are NOT distributed - only YouTube ids.
artifacts.data_license: CC BY 4.0 for the annotations (repo README); the underlying videos remain under YouTube's terms and their uploaders' licences
artifacts.redistributable: annotations yes (CC BY 4.0); videos and extracted frames no
artifacts.notes: Annotations carry no transcripts, so ASR must be regenerated; the paper does not say with what. The release is also smaller than the paper: 2,974 of 3,268 questions (91.0%) and 2,189 of 2,405 videos, so even a perfect re-run is a different, partly overlapping item set and a further unknown share of those YouTube ids will have gone private or been removed since. No per-item GPT-4o outputs were released, so the comparison would be accuracy-level only.

blockers: Video/image input beyond the text-only runner, with no paper code to lean on: the repository contains no evaluation, frame-extraction, ASR or request-building code whatsoever, so every multimodal step would be our own re-implementation rather than the authors' pipeline.

The 2,189 videos must be pulled from YouTube, which is a terms-of-service question and an availability-drift problem on top of it; the annotation release has itself already shrunk to 91% of the paper's item count (2,974 / 3,268).

Cost: roughly $166 for a single seed at default image detail (see budget), far above the ~$30 ceiling for a multimodal card, and about $45 even if all eight frames are sent at low detail - which would itself be a protocol change.

Three unreported protocol parameters that materially move the number: the frame-sampling rule, the image detail/resolution, and the ASR engine. Choice formatting (letters vs raw option text) is also not printed, and decoding parameters are absent entirely.
The GEM column for this row is computed on 10% of the results (Table 4 caption), so only the accuracy cell is a full-set measurement.

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (P0) - not runnable here, see blockers

dead_comparators_not_runnable: Gemini-1.5-pro-002 and Gemini-1.5-flash (Google retirements; outside the OpenAI census anyway)

budget.assumptions: One seed over the current 2,974-item release. Per call: 8 frames at default (high) detail ~ 1,105 tokens each = ~8,840; ASR transcript for a video of up to 15 minutes ~ 1,500 tokens on average; question + five choices measured from the release at ~253 tokens, plus ~120 tokens of instruction; output ~120 tokens ('[CHOICE]: [REASON]', concise). That is ~10,800 in / ~120 out per call = $0.056, i.e. $166 per seed and ~$498 at the usual 3 seeds. Sending all eight frames at low detail (85 tokens each) would cut it to about $45 per seed but changes the protocol. MMH alone (1,074 items) would be ~$60 per seed.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (not executable as specified). Had it been runnable: primary number = NEPTUNE-FULL accuracy for gpt-4o-2024-05-13 on the still-available subset, with coverage reported. Survival = re-run accuracy (median of 3 seeds) inside the bootstrap 95% CI over items of 80.23 (n~2,974, about +/-1.4 pp) AND the ranking claims hold (GPT-4o still comparable to Gemini-1.5-pro, still above LLaVA-OneVision and far above the 20% random floor). Partial = level shifts beyond the CI but the ordering against the open-source block survives. Death = accuracy falls to or below the best open-source long-context model.
judgment.notes: Any re-run is a partial replication by construction: the item set is 91% of the original, the video pixels depend on YouTube availability, and the frames/ASR are ours rather than the authors'. A defensible fallback is to treat the re-run as a NEW measurement on the released subset and report only the direction of the ranking claims, not a level comparison with 80.23.

user_checks: Confirm 'blocked': the paper ships no code at all, so the eight-frame + ASR multimodal pipeline would be entirely our own, and even a single seed is ~$166. Any scope at which you would still want it (e.g. MMH only, low-detail frames, ~$60)?

If a text-only shadow arm is of interest instead, the paper's own ASR-only ablation (Table 3) gives a text-only reference point for Gemini and VideoLLaMA2 - but not for GPT-4o, so it would be a new measurement rather than a re-execution.
domain_notes: Tier B relationship: harness/tierb/configs/W4405355440.json already carries this paper at prompt level (status needs_human, no hook, est $98) and the triage record harness/tierb/W4405355440.json marks the data as 'partial'. The repository does NOT enable an upgrade to repository-based re-execution - it is a data-and-README repository with no code, so the prompt-level config remains the only available protocol. Two corrections to the Tier B record: (1) the annotations are in fact publicly downloadable - the README's storage.mtls.* link is sign-in gated but the plain storage.googleapis.com/neptunedata/ URLs serve both JSONs anonymously; (2) the released item counts are 2,974 / 1,074, not the paper's 3,268 / 1,171, so the Tier B n_items of 3,268 is unattainable and the cost estimate should scale down accordingly (while the per-call cost estimate of $0.03 looks low for eight default-detail frames).
decisions_2026_09_19: status blocked: multimodal input with no author code, YouTube dependence, and a one-seed cost of ~$166
record the public GCS URLs and the shrunken release counts as corrections to the Tier B config
